title: Eval signature and confidence scaling for config rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: Introduce an "evaluation signature" and a calibrated confidence scaling layer for LLM-as-judge outputs to reduce noisy regression alerts and enable safer, automated config/model rollouts.
background: When a model or serving configuration changes we currently compare eval scores on reference prompt sets and run threshold-based guard rails. This approach produces two classes of failures: (1) spurious alerts due to changes in score distribution across model families or prompt slices, and (2) missed regressions when the judge's raw outputs are poorly calibrated for probability-based gating.

Existing experiments (see PM-8321 and PM-9128) show calibration drift across model families and that ensemble voting reduces variance but is expensive to run for every candidate rollout. We need a lighter-weight, systematic way to characterize the change and convert judge outputs into stable probabilities to drive rollouts and alerts.
proposal: Define an immutable 'evaluation signature' for each roll candidate consisting of: short config fingerprint (model id + quantization profile + runtime flags), a small, fixed provenance sample of prompts (100-300 per target workload), and dataset slice histograms (length, instruction type). The signature is recorded by CI for each build.

Produce historical delta distributions for signature families: maintain a compact summary (mean, std, 95% CI) of past score shifts per signature family to set adaptive alert thresholds instead of fixed absolute thresholds.

Add a 'confidence scaling' stage for judge outputs: use a dedicated calibration dataset per signature family and apply lightweight calibration (temperature scaling or isotonic regression) to map raw judge scores or label probabilities to calibrated probabilities. Persist calibration parameters keyed by signature family and model major-version.

Introduce 'agreement-weighted judge ensemble': combine the primary LLM judge, a smaller fast judge, and deterministic scorers (BLEU-like or rule checks) into a weighted consensus where each element's weight is dynamic and learned from recent calibration data. This lowers cost by using the fast judge/deterministic scorers to veto high-confidence cases and only invoking the expensive judge for borderline examples.

Expose new rollout gating rules in Console: severity buckets (minor/major/blocker) derived from calibrated probability and expected ROI costs. Canary policies should accept candidates only if calibrated probability of no-regression >= configured SLO (e.g., 0.99 for blocker-level, 0.95 for major).

Instrument alerting and post-roll monitoring: create per-signature drift detectors and require an automated recalibration job when drift crosses threshold. Log all eval signatures and calibration parameter versions to audit logs for postmortem.
acceptance_criteria: Evaluation signature is computed and stored by CI for every rollout candidate and surfaced in the PR summary (stored as signature_id).

Calibration pipeline produces per-signature parameters and an API to apply scaling to judge outputs; Brier score on held-out calibration sets improves by >= 20% for at least two signature families compared to uncalibrated baseline.
Adaptive thresholding based on historical delta reduces false-positive regression alerts by >= 30% on historical test set (compare to fixed-threshold baseline).
Console shows calibrated probability and severity bucket in the rollout preview and enforces the configured canary gating rule for internal canaries (no manual overrides for blocker-level failures).
Cost target: average extra evaluator invocation cost <= 15% for the pilot workload by relying on fast-judge short-circuiting for >= 60% of examples.

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overfitting calibration parameters to stale signatures. Mitigation: require time-windowed validation and automatic expiration of calibration params after X days.

Risk: Signature collisions (different configs with same fingerprint). Mitigation: include model family + semantic config hash and provenance sample id to reduce collisions; add warning if collision detected.
Risk: Increased evaluation cost. Mitigation: use agreement-weighted ensemble and fast-judge short-circuit; monitor cost and add budget guardrails in Console.
Risk: Complexity in rollout policy configuration leading to operator errors. Mitigation: ship sane defaults and pre-flight checks; add visible recommended SLOs per workload.
notes: We should coordinate with Privacy/Security for any persisted prompt provenance — no raw customer prompts should be stored; only hashed provenance and metadata are allowed.
Start pilot with two internal workloads (chat assistant and search-rewrite) that represent different length distributions.
Plan for a two-week bake period after canary where drift detectors run every 6 hours before full rollout.
